text:
WEIERSTRASS ELLIPTIC AND RELATED FUNCTIONS (p.631)
18.2. Homogeneity Relations, Reduction Formulas and Processes
Homogeneity Relations (Suppose t\neq 0)
Note that Period Ratio is preserved.
18.2.1  \wp'(tz|t\omega,t\omega')=t^{-3}\wp'(z|\omega,\omega')
18.2.2  \wp(tz|t\omega,t\omega')=t^{-2}\wp(z|\omega,\omega')
18.2.3  \zeta(tz|t\omega,t\omega')=t^{-1}\zeta(z|\omega,\omega')
18.2.4  \sigma(tz|t\omega,t\omega')=t\sigma(z|\omega,\omega')
18.2.5  g_2(t\omega,t\omega')=t^{-4}g_2(\omega,\omega')
18.2.6  g_3(t\omega,t\omega')=t^{-6}g_3(\omega,\omega')
18.2.7  e_i(t\omega,t\omega')=t^{-2}e_i(\omega,\omega'), i=1,2,3
18.2.8  \Delta(t\omega,t\omega')=t^{-12}\Delta(\omega,\omega')
18.2.9  H_i(t\omega,t\omega')=t^{-2}H_i(\omega,\omega'), i=1,2,3  (See 18.3)
18.2.10  q(t\omega,t\omega')=q(\omega,\omega')  (See 18.10)
18.2.11  m(t\omega,t\omega')=m(\omega,\omega')  (See 18.9)
18.2.12  \wp'(tz;t^{-4}g_2,t^{-6}g_3)=t^{-3}\wp'(z;g_2,g_3)
18.2.13  \wp(tz;t^{-4}g_2,t^{-6}g_3)=t^{-2}\wp(z;g_2,g_3)
18.2.14  \zeta(tz;t^{-4}g_2,t^{-6}g_3)=t^{-1}\zeta(z;g_2,g_3)
18.2.15  \sigma(tz;t^{-4}g_2,t^{-6}g_3)=t\sigma(z;g_2,g_3)
The Case g_3<0
Put t=i and obtain, e.g.,
18.2.16  \wp(z;g_2,g_3)=-\wp(iz;g_2,-g_3)
Thus the case g_3<0 can be reduced to one where g_3>0.
"Period" Relations and Reduction to the FPP (M,N integers)
18.2.17  \wp'(z+2M\omega+2N\omega')=\wp'(z)
18.2.18  \wp(z+2M\omega+2N\omega')=\wp(z)
18.2.19  \zeta(z+2M\omega+2N\omega')=\zeta(z)+2M\eta+2N\eta'
18.2.20  \sigma(z+2M\omega+2N\omega')=(-1)^{M+N+MN}\sigma(z)\exp[(z+M\omega+N\omega')(2M\eta+2N\eta')]
18.2.21  where \eta=\zeta(\omega), \eta'=\zeta(\omega')
"Conjugate" Values
f(\bar z)=\bar f(z), where f is any one of the functions \wp, \wp', \zeta, \sigma.
Reduction to 1/4 FPP (See Figure 18.1)
(\bar s denotes conjugate of s)
Two sub-columns below, \Delta>0 (left) and \Delta<0 (right):
Point z_4 in R_4
18.2.22  [\Delta>0] \wp'(z_4)=-\overline{\wp'}(2\omega-z_4)   |   [\Delta<0] \wp'(\bar z_4)=-\overline{\wp'}(2\omega_2-z_4)
18.2.23  [\Delta>0] \wp(z_4)=\overline{\wp}(2\omega-z_4)   |   [\Delta<0] \wp(z_4)=\overline{\wp}(2\omega_2-z_4)
18.2.24  [\Delta>0] \zeta(z_4)=-\overline{\zeta}(2\omega-z_4)+2\eta   |   [\Delta<0] \zeta(z_4)=-\overline{\zeta}(2\omega_2-z_4)+2(\eta+\eta')
18.2.25  [\Delta>0] \sigma(z_4)=\overline{\sigma}(2\omega-z_4)\exp[2\eta(z_4-\omega)]   |   [\Delta<0] \sigma(z_4)=\overline{\sigma}(2\omega_2-z_4)\exp[2(\eta+\eta')(z_4-\omega_2)]
Point z_3 in R_3
18.2.26  \wp'(z_3)=-\wp'(2\omega_2-z_3)   (same formula printed identically in both the \Delta>0 and \Delta<0 sub-columns)
18.2.27  \wp(z_3)=\wp(2\omega_2-z_3)   (same in both sub-columns)
18.2.28  \zeta(z_3)=-\zeta(2\omega_2-z_3)+2(\eta+\eta')   (same in both sub-columns)
18.2.29  \sigma(z_3)=\sigma(2\omega_2-z_3)\exp[2(\eta+\eta')(z_3-\omega_2)]   (same in both sub-columns)
Point z_2 in R_2
18.2.30  [\Delta>0] \wp'(z_2)=\overline{\wp'}(\bar z_2-2\omega')   |   [\Delta<0] \wp'(z_2)=\overline{\wp'}(\bar z_2)
18.2.31  [\Delta>0] \wp(z_2)=\overline{\wp}(\bar z_2-2\omega')   |   [\Delta<0] \wp(z_2)=\overline{\wp}(\bar z_2)
18.2.32  [\Delta>0] \zeta(z_2)=\overline{\zeta}(\bar z_2-2\omega')+2\eta'   |   [\Delta<0] \zeta(z_2)=\overline{\zeta}(\bar z_2)
18.2.33  [\Delta>0] \sigma(z_2)=-\overline{\sigma}(\bar z_2-2\omega')\exp[2\eta'(z_2-\omega')]   |   [\Delta<0] \sigma(z_2)=\overline{\sigma}(\bar z_2)
